title: Guesnon on his demands as a musician, his writing, and his domestic arrangements
summary: He insists he is genuine, lists his compositions and writings, says he stays home if not paid properly, and explains why he cannot marry the woman he has been with for 24 years.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well, I mean, you know, I'm just a person like I'm saying. You see, what I'm telling you all this is, because I want you to sit down and understand why my actions are the way they are. You see, there's some people in this life who want as much as me, but they're phonies. But I want what I want because I am for real, I'm no phony. I'm a composer, I'm a musician, I've written over 300 musical compositions, like I told you, four or five short stories, two complete full-length novels, and a book of poems. All right, with all the music and jazz that I play, I know I should demand something when it comes within the bounds of logic and reason and get it. You know what I mean? So if I don't get it, I sit at home. You're going to say that, well, I'm no more or no less than no one else. Well, I disagree. I work harder to gain more, and I want a little more. I don't get it to you, the more I pay it, so I sit at home. You see what I mean? It's just that simple. I don't know what tomorrow's going to bring, but one thing, I never was afraid of tomorrow. You see, I don't know if you was in here, I think you was in here taking a lesson when my old lady passed out again, brought me that little jar with some stew in it. Well, you see, I'm already married, I've got a married wife in California, but the one coming here, I've been going with her 24 years. But we can't get married on account, I belong, I'm a Catholic. Yeah, yeah. You see, and she's in, so I mean, we just stay. Yes, stuff
